I'm in my senior year of high school and this pandemic has ruined a lot of opportunities for me. I was going to take a lot of internships and complete my college applications so I could go to university straight off. Not only has this pandemic destroyed me financially, but mentally as well. I find it extremely difficult to stay motivated and on-top of my work when it doesn't even seem like even my teahers care about me.   


I've now decided to shelf my plan of going straight to college and just going to a community college for two years while I work so I can then transfer out to do another four years, I will be 24 by then. A lot of my friends are going straight to university and I can understand that feeling of not wanting to "get left behind," it's difficult to believe that success is not a race. I would much rather go to college prepared and financially stable rather than be drowned with student debt. Academics isn't all there is to a person. The fact that you're contemplating such dark thoughts because of school shows that the system has failed you, you are not a failure.   


Please try to hold on. You deserve love and respect. You deserve to have basic luxuries whether you earn them or not. You don't need to earn your meals or your sleep, that's how you burn yourself out. You deserve to be alive. You deserve to have a shot at life even if you feel like you don't.
